solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Battle-axe's reward to cuddle sweetheart: time to use delaying tactics!

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold something close in the middle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a battle-axe is a fierce, domineering woman, informally a dragon; the possessive adds S
the heart, or middle letter, of the word sweet is E
a fee is a payment or reward for a service

explanation.surface: A formidable woman gets her payoff for hugging a loved one, then stalls for time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is not a lover but the middle letter of 'sweet'; 'to cuddle' puts it inside the dragon's reward. The answer splits as DRAG ONE'S FEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to drag one's feet is to be deliberately slow, stalling progress on purpose.

clue.text: Last of sediment hauled up to take away

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are written bottom to top, so they read backwards
the last of a word is its final letter, here the end of sediment

parts.note: to haul goods by cart is to have carted them

explanation.surface: Someone drags the final dregs of silt upwards to remove them.
explanation.walkthrough: T plus CARTED, read upwards as the entry goes down, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to detract from something is to take away from its value or worth.

clue.text: Price going up?

parts.note: looks like inflation, a rising cost, but means the cost of going up into the sky on a flight

explanation.surface: A query about whether costs are rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' suggests inflation; read literally it is what one pays to go up in a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: a ticket for a flight is the price paid to travel up through the sky.

clue.text: One's experienced chafing down below wearing tight leotards

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the shuffled letters are worn round the single letter
tight is slang for drunk, and drunk letters reel into a new order
in a down entry the bottom of a word is its final letter, here the end of chafing

explanation.surface: A dancer finds snug gymnastic outfits rubbing uncomfortably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' describes the leotards in the surface but signals the anagram. G, the bottom of 'chafing', goes inside the reworked LEOTARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is a veteran, someone long practised and seasoned in an activity.

clue.text: More than one test paper cut up first

indicators.note: first says this reversed piece comes at the start, before the paper
in a down entry, up means the letters run bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a written paper

explanation.surface: A sheet of paper is chopped up before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'test paper' wants to be read together, but the definition stops at 'test'; MS (manuscript) is the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun: these are formal tests, so several of them are more than one test.

clue.text: Charlie brings articles into fashion

indicators.note: into means the second piece is placed inside the first

parts.note: a fad is a passing fashion or craze
the and a are the definite and indefinite articles

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie introduces new items into the clothing trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a name; in British slang a charlie is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: in British usage a charlie is a silly person, a dimwit or idiot.

clue.text: Very important office's opening in new chapel

indicators.note: in means the single letter is placed inside the rearranged letters
making something new means remaking it, so these letters are rearranged
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The start of a church service takes place in a recently built chapel, a significant event.
explanation.definitionFit: Something epochal marks a new era, so it is momentous and highly significant.

clue.text: Means of securing the basics

definitions.meaning: threaded fasteners and their matching parts hold things together
idiom for the practical fundamentals of a subject

explanation.surface: A way to make something safe is the fundamentals.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally hardware fasteners; figuratively the essential practical details of anything.

clue.text: How bread may appear cut initially, it's said

indicators.note: cutting a word initially means removing its first letter

parts.note: bread spread with butter appears buttered

explanation.surface: A description of how sliced bread might look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' suggests slicing the loaf; it removes the first letter of BUTTERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something uttered has been spoken, so it is said aloud.

clue.text: Music possibly encapsulated by Mozart, for many

indicators.note: encapsulated by means held inside these words, so the letters run across them

explanation.surface: To many people, Mozart sums up music.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: music is one kind of creative discipline, alongside painting or poetry; 'possibly' flags the example.

clue.text: Parisian girl produced wine, one bottled

parts.note: to have produced something is to have made it

indicators.note: bottled means put inside, so the single letter goes into the wine

parts.note: Moselle is a German white wine from the Mosel valley
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone made wine and bottled one batch.
explanation.definitionFit: French title for an unmarried woman, so a young woman of Paris.

clue.text: Marine animal and insect getting closer?

parts.note: a seal is a sea mammal
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A sea creature and a bug approach each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closer' reads as nearer; here it is one that closes up gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Function: a sealing compound closes up cracks and joints, so it is a thing that closes.

clue.text: Clock heads for third hour, egg duly boiled!

parts.note: to clock is informal for to notice or see

indicators.note: heads for means taking the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Watch the clock until the third hour: then the egg has been properly cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock' looks like a timepiece but is a verb, to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: water that seethed bubbled and churned, as when it boiled.

clue.text: Salt on after egg

indicators.note: after says the piece for on comes behind the piece for egg

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Seasoning is added once the egg is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' is a louse's egg, not a hen's.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a chemical salt.

clue.text: Nan and mother, squeezing first of sponges, left wiping the floor with the others

definitions.text: wiping the floor with the others

parts.note: nan and gran are both informal words for a grandmother

indicators.note: squeezing means holding tightly within, so the letters go inside

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Grandma and Mum cram in a sponge cake before leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word. In the surface 'wiping the floor' sounds like cleaning; it means beating everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning every major event in a season means you have beaten every rival comprehensively.

clue.text: Narrative too orderly about European Community, full stop!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer piece goes round the inner

parts.note: anal is informal for fussily obsessed with order and detail
a full stop, the punctuation mark, is a dot

explanation.surface: A tale of a fussy official round Brussels, end of story.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: based on personal stories rather than data, so told as a narrative.

clue.text: Restaurant in old club welcoming sovereign

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: a brassie is an old name for a golf club, the two-wood
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the sovereign

explanation.surface: A restaurant in a historic gentlemen's club lets in a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old club' is a golf club, not a society. ER is Queen Elizabeth's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Type of eatery: a French-style informal dining place serving simple food.

clue.text: America doesn't need me to drink a black coffee

indicators.note: to drink means taking in, so the letters go inside
not needing something means doing without it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The States can do without me ordering a black coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking ME from AMERICA leaves ARICA, which takes in A and B (black).
explanation.definitionFit: Variety: the main species of coffee bean grown commercially worldwide.

clue.text: Cunning insult overheard?

indicators.note: overheard means caught by ear, so it is the sound of the word that counts

parts.note: a slight is a snub or insult

explanation.surface: Was that a clever dig I just caught?
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means dexterous trickery or craftiness, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Isle in better state

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: An island in improved condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better state' reads as an improved condition; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Old ship, one docking?

definitions.meaning: to dock is to cut short, so one who trims is a docker

explanation.surface: A historic vessel coming into port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docking' suggests a ship berthing; here it means cutting, as of a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast sailing ship of old, and also a person or tool that trims or cuts short.

clue.text: Mother dear holds precedence

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: dear means expensive, pricy
ma is informal for mother

explanation.surface: A loving mother takes priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dear' looks like a term of affection; it means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being first in rank or importance, taking priority over others.

clue.text: Home behind field that's most unproductive

indicators.note: behind says the home piece goes after the field piece

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field, a poetic word
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A house stands behind the poorest-yielding field.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean years or land yield little, so the leanest are the least fruitful.

clue.text: Note something invigorating

definitions.meaning: the keynote or first degree of a musical scale
a drink or medicine that refreshes or restores

explanation.surface: Remark on a refreshing pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the home note of a key; in general a restorative pick-me-up.

clue.text: Most unholy of sins? Choose to embrace one

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: to choose is to decide
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Picking which wrongdoing is the very worst one.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing a god would be the ultimate blasphemy, hence the most impious possible crime.

clue.text: Taste insect in tin

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a midge is a small fly

explanation.surface: Sampling a bug found in a can.
explanation.walkthrough: SN is tin's chemical symbol, from Latin stannum.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tiny amount, as in just a taste or a little bit.

clue.text: Wave spoilt a sheet of canvas

indicators.note: to wave hair is to set it in new curls, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A bad breaker ruined a tarpaulin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' looks like the sea or a noun; it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sail set above the lowest one on a mast, a sheet of canvas on a ship.

clue.text: Very much in detail?

definitions.meaning: point by point, item by item, specifically

explanation.surface: Greatly and thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: Means especially, and also in a detailed way, one specific point at a time.
